dedupe_keys.name: nyc green infrastructure program for combined sewer overflow reduction 2021 annual report

description: The NYC Green Infrastructure Program retrofits streets, sidewalks and public and private properties across New York City with rain gardens and other green infrastructure to reduce combined sewer overflows into New York Harbor, while adding co-benefits such as less local flooding, urban greening and heat reduction. It covers the city's combined sewer areas, with strategic projects in separately sewered areas, and the 2021 annual report records that DEP certified 1,181 greened acres and 507 million gallons per year of overflow reduction from over 9,100 constructed assets for its 1.5 per cent application-rate milestone, toward a 2030 goal of 1.67 billion gallons per year. It is run by the New York City Department of Environmental Protection with the Economic Development Corporation, Design and Construction, Transportation and Parks departments, and had committed over 1.09 billion dollars in capital funds since fiscal year 2012. The 74-page report is available as a free PDF download on the DEP website, with earlier reports and the Green Infrastructure Plan; no licence is stated. Caveats: figures are programme-reported and the report describes 2021 status. It is a reference case for city-scale green-blue stormwater infrastructure, adaptive management and maintenance at scale for climate adaptation; a related record is the Augustenborg Malmö stormwater case study.
